In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of when and how people may decide not to share third party information, and we propose to study the conditions under which the spread of information is inhibited by a normative goal frame.
the conditions under which individuals refrain from gossiping.
the microfoundations of gossiping and the conditions under which gossip is not shared.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the decision of whether to share information about an absent target with another individual depends on the nature of the information, the relationship with the receiver, and the relationship with the target, as well as on the goals and frames of the gossip sender.

the spread of gossip is a complex process in which the costs and benefits of gossiping are not only a function of the information to be shared, but also of the relations between the actors in the gossiping dyad and of the goal frames they hold.

gossip is not always good, nor is silence always bad, and that the conditions in which gossip is shared and the reasons for which gossip is withheld may be as important as the content of the information that is shared or not shared.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
silence is golden in the context of gossip.
the spread of gossip is not only driven by the pleasure of gossiping but also by its costs.
the costs of gossip may be higher than previously assumed and the conditions under which gossip is shared may be far more complex than the literature on gossip suggests.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the decision not to share gossip is not only a consequence of the absence of the opportunity to do so but rather a deliberate and strategic choice that may be influenced by the content of the information, the context of its sharing, and the relations between the actors involved in the gossip triadic exchange.
a goal framing approach can be used to better understand the microfoundations of gossiping and the conditions under which it may be inhibited.
a more complete understanding of why and when people do not gossip is necessary to fully appreciate the role that gossiping plays in human social life.
